summary: Arizona advances a 36-MMBF Good Neighbor project, Louisiana Green Fuels selects biomass technology, Minnesota aerial-seeds 500 acres, western timber auctions open, and TP&EE starts tomorrow.
socialText: Arizona puts an estimated 36 MMBF into a new GNA pipeline; Louisiana Green Fuels selects technology for a biomass market designed around 3.5M+ tons/year; western auction week opens.
cardTeaser: Arizona puts an estimated 36 MMBF into a new GNA pipeline
cardSubhead: Nearly 14,000 acres of restoration work pairs federal and utility funding with commercial timber and reinvested sale revenue.
strikingText: Louisiana Green Fuels' current full-build design would consume more than 3.5 million tons of forestry residuals a year—roughly 400 truckloads a day. At that scale, feedstock logistics are not support work; they are the project.

summary: Diesel reaches $6.285 per gallon, November lumber closes at $537, a base-oil shortage raises maintenance costs, and a new free forest-risk platform brings wildfire, drought and pest data together.
socialText: Diesel hits $6.285/gal while November lumber closes at $537; lubricant costs are rising; a new free forest-risk platform combines wildfire, drought and pest data.
cardTeaser: Diesel hits $6.285 as November lumber slides to $537
cardSubhead: Fuel is pushing operating costs higher while the most visible softwood benchmark moved 7.2% lower in a week.
strikingText: Diesel jumped 31.8¢ in one week to $6.285/gal while November lumber fell 7.2% to $537/MBF. Forest businesses are getting squeezed from both directions: higher operating costs and a weaker product-price signal.

summary: Conifex secures up to C$30 million for Mackenzie, Flathead clears 3,726 acres of commercial treatment, Mississippi expands cross-boundary forestry, and Roadless Rule comments move to October 6.
socialText: Conifex lands up to C$30M for Mackenzie; Montana clears 3,726 acres of commercial treatment; Mississippi puts markets and GNA work inside a new stewardship framework.
cardTeaser: Conifex lands up to C$30 million for Mackenzie
cardSubhead: The financing backs a planned return to two-shift sawmill production — with another C$11 million available for performance-focused capital work.
strikingText: Conifex now has access to up to C$30 million in federal tariff financing for Mackenzie, plus as much as C$11 million for performance-focused capital work. That is a meaningful amount of runway behind a planned two-shift restart.

summary: Nackawic plans a 190,000-tonne pulp idle, Washington carries unsold timber into auction week, a Pennsylvania logging business liquidates, and Minnesota's North Star Expo continues.
socialText: Nackawic plans to idle 190,000 tonnes/year of dissolving-pulp capacity; Washington carries 13+ MMBF of unsold timber into auction week; a Pennsylvania logging business liquidates.
cardTeaser: Nackawic plans to idle 190,000 tonnes of annual pulp capacity
cardSubhead: The New Brunswick mill had already stopped buying wood in August; roughly 350 workers face the end-October shutdown.

summary: Ashland doubles sawmill capacity, Saint John receives NextGen equipment, Ontario backs biomass demand, South Carolina offers pine, and B.C. cuts its stumpage forecast.
socialText: Ashland is doubling toward 250 MMBF; Ontario backs projects creating 130,000+ tonnes of annual biomass demand; B.C. cuts expected Crown stumpage to C$13.55/m³.
cardSubhead: The northern Maine expansion adds 120 million board feet of annual sawmill capacity—and a larger pull on the regional wood basket.
strikingText: Ontario is spending just over $2.5 million on three projects that could create demand for more than 130,000 tonnes of forest biomass a year. Small public dollars can matter when they unlock a much larger fibre market.

summary: Fort Drum timber closes today, southern pine thinnings reach bid day, B.C. expands community-forest fibre, and Idaho and Montana state timber auctions open.
socialText: Fort Drum puts 312 acres to bid today; three Arkansas pine thinnings totaling ~332 acres close this afternoon; B.C. adds 28,100+ m³ of annual community-forest fibre.
cardTeaser: Three Arkansas pine thinnings close today
cardSubhead: About 332 acres across Miller, Little River and Ouachita counties hit the bid deadline this afternoon.
strikingText: B.C. is adding more than 28,100 m³ of annual fibre to two community forests. The interesting shift is not just more wood—it is more fibre moving through locally controlled tenure.

summary: Twain Lumber revives Virginia sawmill capacity, Pennsylvania and Mississippi timber sales close, B.C. tests a working-forest model, and southern capacity growth puts utilization in focus.
socialText: Virginia is bringing 108 MMBF of sawmill capacity back; ~1.27 MMBF of Pennsylvania hardwood closes today; B.C. picks Campbell River for its first three-zone working-forest test.
cardTeaser: Virginia brings a shuttered sawmill back toward 108 MMBF
cardSubhead: Twain Lumber plans more than $51.2 million of Virginia-grown forest-product purchases in its first three years.
strikingText: Forisk projects 2.1 BBF of net new southern sawmill capacity through 2028 while Q1 North American production remained 4% below a year earlier. More iron does not solve a utilization problem.

summary: Témiscaming shuts down today, Idaho's Top Hat sale approaches, a North Carolina timber-market directory targets transaction friction, and forest-products and hardwood market gatherings open this week.
socialText: Témiscaming shuts down today; Idaho's Top Hat timber sale is eight days from bids; a North Carolina directory is trying to make timber buyers, foresters and loggers easier to find.
cardTeaser: Témiscaming's indefinite shutdown takes effect today
cardSubhead: Roughly 400 unionized jobs—and a wider Quebec–Ontario fibre and contractor network—are exposed.
strikingText: North Carolina's TimberClear has 247 timber-industry listings across 25 towns, including 82 buyers and 154 consulting foresters. For small timber sellers, finding the market may be as much a bottleneck as price.

summary: South Carolina timber bids open tomorrow, Maine forestry disaster relief remains available, Quebec wood-innovation funding closes Friday, Oregon enters state-timber bid week, and Canada refreshes public forest-product pricing.
socialText: South Carolina opens an ~8,100-ton state-forest sale tomorrow; Maine has $60M in disaster relief that includes timber losses; Quebec wood-innovation funding closes Friday.
cardTeaser: About 8,100 tons of South Carolina timber opens for bids tomorrow
cardSubhead: The 79-acre Sand Hills sale is pine-dominant, all-weather and includes a separate chip bid.
strikingText: Maine’s $60 million disaster-relief program explicitly covers both standing and harvested timber losses—and reimburses the licensed-forester cost required to document a timber claim.

summary: Pennsylvania hardwood timber sales approach, Virginia logging equipment moves through the secondary market, Témiscaming prepares for an indefinite shutdown, Canadian exporters court international buyers, and CAL FIRE refreshes treatment-effectiveness data.
socialText: Pennsylvania puts nearly 2 MMBF of hardwood timber up September 23; logging equipment moves through a Virginia liquidation; Témiscaming's paperboard and high-yield pulp shutdown arrives Monday.
cardTeaser: Nearly 2 MMBF of Pennsylvania hardwood goes to bid September 23
cardSubhead: Elk and Huntingdon County sales offer a paired read on northern Appalachian demand.
strikingText: RYAM’s Témiscaming shutdown puts roughly 425 jobs at risk and removes a major western Quebec fibre outlet indefinitely. The bigger forestry problem is not the mill gate—it is where that wood goes next.

summary: Oregon gains new state-forest regulatory certainty, Idaho advertises an 8,385-MBF sale, lumber pricing firms, Weyerhaeuser leases geothermal rights, and a new PNW silviculture review maps changing mill and management realities.
socialText: Oregon gains state-forest ESA certainty; Idaho puts 8,385 MBF on the block; a new PNW review shows mill infrastructure feeding directly back into silviculture.
strikingText: Private lands now supply roughly 75% of westside PNW annual harvest, while only a handful of mills still buy logs over 60 cm on the small end. Mill infrastructure is no longer just processing the silviculture - it is shaping it.

summary: Rising global wood demand meets tougher traceability requirements, California opens working-forest project funding, western timber auctions approach, and sawmill AI and vision systems move deeper into operations.
socialText: Wood demand is projected to rise 37% by 2050 as traceability reshapes trade; CAL FIRE opens working-forest project funding; sawmill AI and vision systems push optimization deeper into operations.
strikingText: Global wood demand is projected to rise 37% by 2050 just as traceability rules require much finer proof of origin. For timber and pulp suppliers, chain-of-custody data is becoming part of the product, not just paperwork.

summary: Colorado's largest sawmill enters a 60-day buyer search, USITC issues a final hardwood-plywood injury determination, a new Forest Service road-risk dataset goes national, and major Virginia and B.C. timber sales close today.
socialText: Colorado's largest sawmill has 60 days to find a buyer as logging capacity leaks away; USITC reaches a final hardwood-plywood decision; new USFS data maps road erosion risk nationwide.
strikingText: Montrose Forest Products is not just racing a 60-day WARN clock. Six of eight logging contractors that had supplied Colorado's largest sawmill have already found work elsewhere. A buyer would be acquiring a mill and a contractor-rebuilding problem.

summary: Diesel pressure on loggers, Washington EAB management guidance, unsold state timber sales, a Texas government timber sale, lumber-distribution consolidation, and updated field tools.
socialText: Diesel is squeezing loggers without full surcharges; Washington shifts from EAB preparation to active management; three recent DNR timber sales remain unsold at minimum value.
strikingText: The fuel problem is no longer just price: log haulers may be absorbing diesel increases that ordinary freight carriers pass through with surcharges. That can turn marginal haul distance into a procurement constraint.

summary: Arkansas mill-siting research, Mercer Peace River downtime, Enstructure's LOGISTEC acquisition, Forest Service research-office changes, and industrial-wood auction opportunities.
socialText: Arkansas maps optimal new mill sites; Mercer Peace River takes 15,000 ADMT of planned downtime; Enstructure folds LOGISTEC into a 106-terminal North American network.
strikingText: Mercer Peace River’s 10-day outage takes 15,000 ADMT offline—about 1,500 tonnes/day—while bringing 475–500 contractors on site. Maintenance at one pulp mill briefly becomes a regional labor and wood-flow event.

summary: B.C. cuts TFL 30's AAC 17.6%, Pennsylvania hardwood sales close this week, Pacific Northwest federal auctions bunch up after Labor Day, and a 4,833-acre Washington timber portfolio remains active.
socialText: B.C. cuts TFL 30's AAC 17.6%; Pennsylvania offers a 692-MBF oak sale Wednesday; a 4,833-acre Washington timber portfolio is still active after its original bid date.
strikingText: B.C. just cut TFL 30's allowable annual cut 17.6% to 340,000 m³—and explicitly removed more economically marginal ground from the harvestable land base. Fibre supply is contracting not just biologically, but economically.

summary: LP's Jasper OSB curtailment, Southern log-trucking entry barriers, Oregon timberland pricing, hardwood slab data, forest-road research, and field tools.
socialText: LP is idling 475M sq. ft. of Jasper OSB capacity; a 573-driver Southern study puts insurance and experience at the center of the log-truck bottleneck; a 1,120-acre Oregon timber tract asks $5.7M.
strikingText: About 80% of Southern log-truck drivers surveyed don't want to leave the business, yet only 9% of non-third-party drivers would consider third-party hauling without better pay and benefits. The bottleneck looks more like entry economics than retention.

summary: Washington salvage authority, Coosa Pines pulpwood impacts, Tahoe Forest Products financing, lumber prices, Western contractor opportunities, WOTUS, and new tools.
socialText: Washington lifts fast-track salvage sales to $2M; Coosa Pines' closure sends pine pulpwood stumpage toward zero; Tahoe Forest Products lands $50M in USDA-backed financing.

summary: Forest Service research closures, Espanola restart engineering, J.D. Irving gatewood prices, Minnesota red-pine cones, Pisgah contracting, and new publications.
Ontario biomass investment, the Témiscaming shutdown, southern treating capacity, hardwood exports to India, gatewood pricing, and the GATES trucking-cost tool.
